qt: to the Commission Benoit Cassart (Renew) Subject:

Earlier this year, in a letter to MEPs, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that the Commission acknowledged the role that higher biofuel blends can play in decarbonising the existing vehicle fleet and that it would look into enabling higher ethanol blends, such as E20, as part of the revision of the policy framework for fuels. On 22 September 2026, Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra confirmed this in his reply to Written Question E002866/20261. Given the significant emission reduction benefits that may be achieved through the greater use of renewable ethanol made in Europe (emissions on average 81.6 % lower than with fossil petrol) and the growing interest in higher ethanol blends, could the Commission clarify the following points: 1.
Does the Commission intend to propose a revision of the Fuel Quality Directive to enable E20 in the current institutional term?

According to what indicative timetable does it plan to deliver such a proposal, so that the potential decarbonisation and energy sovereignty benefits of E20 can be realised in a sustainable, affordable and time-relevant manner?
